# Hypothetical Therapy Session: Client Statements

## Client Backstory

**Name:** Marcus Chen, 34 years old

**Background:** Marcus is a former software engineer at a promising tech startup in Seattle. Eighteen months ago, the company he helped build from the ground up was acquired by a larger corporation, and he was laid off despite being one of the founding team members. He's been unemployed for 14 months, living off severance and savings that are now nearly depleted.

**Family:** Marcus is married to his wife, Dina, a pediatric nurse who works night shifts. They have a 6-year-old daughter, Lily, and a 3-year-old son, Ethan. His parents immigrated from Taiwan and run a small restaurant in Portland. His relationship with his father has always been strained—his father never approved of Marcus leaving a "stable" engineering job at Boeing to join a startup.

**Current Situation:** Marcus has been experiencing depression and anxiety for the past year. He struggles with insomnia, has withdrawn from friends, and feels tremendous guilt about not contributing financially. He recently had a panic attack at a job interview and left before completing it. His wife encouraged him to start therapy after she found him sitting alone in his car in the garage for two hours, unable to go inside and face his family.

---

## 100 Client Statements

### Opening/General State

1. "I almost didn't come today. I sat in my car for twenty minutes trying to convince myself to walk in."

2. "This week has been... I don't even know how to describe it. Just heavy."

3. "I keep telling myself things will get better, but I don't actually believe it anymore."

4. "Dina thinks I'm making progress, but I feel like I'm just getting better at hiding how bad it really is."

5. "I woke up at 3 AM again every single night this week."

6. "Sometimes I wonder if there's even a point to talking about all this."

7. "I'm so tired of being tired."

8. "I feel like I'm watching my life happen to someone else."

### Employment and Career

9. "I had another interview scheduled for Thursday, but I canceled it. I couldn't go through that again."

10. "Every job posting I see, I convince myself I'm not qualified before I even finish reading it."

11. "It's been fourteen months now. At what point do I just accept that I'm unemployable?"

12. "I used to be good at what I did. I helped build that company. Now I can't even get past a phone screening."

13. "The startup world doesn't want someone in their mid-thirties. They want hungry twenty-five-year-olds who'll work eighty hours a week."

14. "I've sent out 247 applications. I keep a spreadsheet. Two hundred forty-seven rejections or silences."

15. "My old colleague Jason just got promoted to VP at Google. I saw it on LinkedIn and had to close my laptop and just... sit there."

16. "I used to love coding. Now when I sit down to work on a personal project, my mind goes completely blank."

17. "The panic attack at the Microsoft interview—I keep replaying it. The way the interviewer looked at me when I said I needed to leave."

18. "I've started lying on my resume. Adding skills I'm rusty on. It feels like the only way to even get noticed."

19. "What if the best years of my career are already behind me?"

20. "I miss having colleagues. I miss having somewhere to be."

### Financial Stress

21. "We have maybe four months of savings left. After that, I don't know what happens."

22. "Dina picked up extra shifts again this week. She says she doesn't mind, but I see how exhausted she is."

23. "I had to tell Lily we couldn't do her birthday party at the trampoline place this year. The look on her face..."

24. "I check our bank account obsessively. Sometimes ten, fifteen times a day. Like I expect money to magically appear."

25. "We might have to sell the house. The house we bought when everything was going so well."

26. "I found myself calculating how much my life insurance policy would pay out. Not in a... I mean, I wasn't planning anything. But the thought was there."

27. "Every time Dina buys groceries, I look at the receipt and mentally add it to my list of failures."

28. "My father offered to lend us money. I'd rather lose the house than take it."

29. "I can't remember the last time I bought something for myself without feeling guilty."

30. "The credit card bill came. I hid it in my desk drawer without opening it."

### Marriage and Relationship with Dina

31. "Dina and I haven't really talked—like actually talked—in weeks. We just coordinate logistics."

32. "I know she's frustrated with me. She tries not to show it, but I can feel it."

33. "We haven't been intimate in... I don't even want to say how long. I feel like I don't deserve that kind of closeness."

34. "She asked me last week what I did all day, and I couldn't give her a real answer. I don't know what I do all day."

35. "Sometimes I think she'd be better off without me. She could find someone who actually contributes."

36. "I snapped at her yesterday over something stupid—she moved my coffee mug. I apologized, but I could see I hurt her."

37. "She leaves me these little notes before she goes to work. 'I believe in you.' 'We'll get through this.' I can't even look at them."

38. "I'm terrified she's going to leave me. And I'm terrified that I'd understand if she did."

39. "She's carrying everything right now. The job, the kids, the house, and now me. How is that fair to her?"

40. "We used to dream about the future together. Now we just worry about next month."

### Parenting and Children

41. "Lily asked me why I don't go to work like Mommy does. I didn't know what to say."

42. "I yelled at Ethan for spilling juice on my laptop. He's three. He's three years old, and I yelled at him."

43. "I missed Lily's school play last month. I told her I was sick, but really I just couldn't get out of bed."

44. "Sometimes I look at my kids and think, what kind of example am I setting? That when things get hard, you just... crumble?"

45. "Ethan has started asking 'Daddy sad?' every morning. He's three and he can see it."

46. "I used to be the fun parent. The one who built pillow forts and made up silly songs. Now I can barely muster the energy to read them a bedtime story."

47. "What if they remember their childhood as the time when Daddy was always sad and tired?"

48. "Lily drew a picture of our family at school. I'm not in it. She said she forgot to draw me."

49. "I love them so much, but sometimes being around them feels exhausting, and then I hate myself for feeling that way."

50. "The only time I feel okay lately is when I'm helping Lily with her homework. It's the one thing I can still do."

### Relationship with Parents/Father

51. "My dad called last Sunday. I let it go to voicemail. Again."

52. "He said 'I told you so' without actually saying it. That's his specialty."

53. "When I told him about the layoff, there was this pause. This long pause. And then he said, 'Well, Boeing is still hiring.'"

54. "He worked seventy-hour weeks at the restaurant for thirty years to give me opportunities. And I feel like I've wasted all of it."

55. "My mom keeps sending me job listings. Data entry positions. Retail management. She means well, but it feels like even she thinks I can't do what I used to do."

56. "I haven't visited them in eight months. I keep making excuses. I can't face them."

57. "My dad never says he's proud of me. I used to think I didn't need to hear it. Now I realize I've been waiting my whole life."

58. "He still doesn't understand what I actually did for a living. To him, I 'played with computers.'"

59. "Growing up, success meant stability. A government job, a pension, a house. I had all that at Boeing, and I gave it up for a dream."

60. "Sometimes I hear his voice in my head when I'm criticizing myself. It's his voice saying I'm not good enough."

### Physical Symptoms and Sleep

61. "I've gained twenty pounds since the layoff. My clothes don't fit. I've just been wearing the same three sweatpants on rotation."

62. "The insomnia is the worst part. I'm so tired, but my brain won't shut off."

63. "I had another panic attack on Tuesday. My chest got tight, my hands went numb, I was sure I was dying."

64. "I've been getting these headaches. Tension headaches, I think. Like a band squeezing my skull."

65. "Some days I sleep twelve hours and still wake up exhausted."

66. "I've started grinding my teeth at night. Dina can hear it."

67. "I can't remember the last time I exercised. I used to run. I used to actually enjoy running."

68. "My heart races sometimes for no reason. Just sitting there, and suddenly it's pounding."

69. "I've been drinking more. Not a lot, but more than I used to. It's the only thing that quiets my mind at night."

70. "I looked in the mirror this morning and didn't recognize myself. I look ten years older."

### Social Isolation

71. "My best friend Kevin has texted me six times in the past month. I've replied once, with a thumbs up emoji."

72. "I deleted all my social media apps. Seeing everyone else's accomplishments was making it worse."

73. "I used to be the one who organized the guys' poker nights. Now I can't imagine sitting across from them, answering questions about my life."

74. "I ran into a neighbor at the grocery store and told her I was 'consulting.' I don't know why I lied."

75. "I haven't left the house in four days. Until today."

76. "The thought of being around people physically exhausts me."

77. "I used to have so many friends. Where did they all go? Or did I push them away?"

78. "Everyone says 'let me know if you need anything,' but no one actually wants to hear how bad it is."

79. "I've become invisible. I'm just the unemployed guy, the cautionary tale people whisper about."

80. "I ghosted my old coworkers' group chat. Three hundred unread messages. I can't bring myself to open it."

### Cognitive Symptoms and Self-Perception

81. "I can't concentrate on anything anymore. I tried to read a book last week and realized I'd been staring at the same page for twenty minutes."

82. "I feel like I'm stupid now. Like the layoff broke something in my brain."

83. "I have this running list in my head of all my failures. It plays on repeat."

84. "I used to be confident. I used to walk into rooms and know I belonged there. Now I apologize for existing."

85. "Sometimes I think everyone was right about me—that I'm not as smart or talented as I thought I was."

86. "I can't make decisions anymore. Even small ones. What to eat for lunch feels overwhelming."

87. "I've started doubting my memories of when things were good. Was I ever actually happy, or was I just pretending?"

88. "I feel like a fraud. Like everything I accomplished was luck and now the luck has run out."

89. "My thoughts spiral so fast. One minute I'm thinking about a job application, and the next I'm convinced my whole life is meaningless."

90. "I don't know who I am without a job title. I was 'Marcus the engineer.' Now I'm just... nothing."

### Deeper Fears and Existential Concerns

91. "What if this is permanent? What if this is just who I am now?"

92. "I'm thirty-four and I feel like my life is over."

93. "I used to think I was building toward something. Now I feel like I'm just trying not to drown."

94. "There are moments—dark moments—where I think everyone would be better off if I just disappeared."

95. "I'm scared of who I'm becoming. I don't like this person."

96. "What's the point of getting better if the world that broke me is still out there, waiting to do it again?"

97. "I feel like I'm failing at being a human being. At the most basic stuff."

98. "Sometimes I think the universe is trying to tell me something—that I aimed too high and this is my punishment."

99. "I'm terrified that my kids will grow up and remember me like this. Broken. Useless."

100. "I want to feel like myself again. I just don't remember who that is."

---

*Note: These statements represent a hypothetical therapeutic scenario for educational purposes. If you or someone you know is experiencing similar feelings, please reach out to a mental health professional or crisis helpline.*
